title: PRA-JA march blocked in Luanda on 28 January
location: From Largo da ENDE in São Paulo toward the Magnólia event complex in Rangel, Luanda; police reportedly stopped the march before it had advanced 100 metres.
demand_text: The reports do not specify a demand made by the march. A talk on autarquias/local governance was scheduled at the destination, but its topic alone does not establish the march’s demand.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. No total attendance is reported. About 17 reported injuries, including passersby and legislators, and the presence of four National Assembly members in the retrospective account are not crowd counts.
tactic: Attempted march; police reportedly blocked it before it advanced 100 metres and used tear gas.

title.summary: O País and Isto É Notícia report a PRA-JA march; the retrospective USDOS report also describes a peaceful political march on the same date in Luanda.

start_date.summary: All three cards place the action on 28 January 2023.

end_date.summary: The march was reportedly halted before it advanced 100 metres; no physical end time or later disposition is reported.

location.summary: The route is reported from Largo da ENDE in São Paulo toward the Magnólia event complex in Rangel, Luanda.

scope.summary: All accounts place this action in Luanda.

organizer.summary: The march is attributed to PRA-JA-Servir Angola.

demands.summary: The reports do not state a specific march demand. The scheduled talk on local governance is not treated as a demand by marchers.

demand_target.summary: A domestic government or public-policy target is not established in the reports.

participants_min.summary: No numerical lower bound on total attendance is given.

participants_max.summary: No numerical upper bound is given.

participants_estimate.summary: No point estimate is given; injury and legislator counts are not attendance.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The 50-person threshold remains unverified because no total crowd count appears in the reports.

tactic.summary: The group attempted a march; sources report police obstruction and tear gas.

protester_violence.summary: The retrospective account calls the march peaceful, but the reporting does not establish a full account of protester conduct; code remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Police obstruction, tear gas, and batons are reported. Tear gas/obstruction support crowd_dispersal=yes; the report does not specify whether/how anyone was struck by batons, so beatings and the other five dimensions remain unknown.

eligibility.summary: Candidate remains pending_state_target; the march demand/target is unspecified, and attendance also remains below a verified 50-person threshold.

notes: S003 and S025 rely on the same PRA-JA communiqué and are not independent corroboration. S029 retrospectively reports a peaceful political march, four National Assembly members, tear gas/baton dispersal and 17 injuries but does not identify the paragraph’s underlying source. None supplies a total turnout. S019 is not used as evidence: it explicitly credits held source S001 (DW África). S029 also mentions batons but does not specify whether participants were struck or how injuries occurred; beatings remains unknown.
open_questions: What demand did the march itself make, and was it directed at the Angolan government or public policy?
How many people assembled? The 50-person threshold is unverified.
Can an independent contemporaneous source establish the action and resolve the retrospective report’s unidentified origin?
What was the action’s physical end and were there state responses beyond reported dispersal?
Did the reported baton use include striking participants, and how were the 17 injuries caused?

title: Luanda gathering for political prisoners and women vendors, stopped before the planned march
location: Largo das Heroínas and the Largo da Independência area, Luanda; a planned march was to proceed toward the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights.
organizer: Activists and unnamed organizers; Folha 8 quotes Adolfo Campos as an organizer.
demand_text: Reported demands include release of political prisoners, better treatment and an end to persecution of women street vendors, measures addressing poverty, lower prices for basic goods, and improved health services.
demand_target: Angolan authorities and domestic policy, as described in the reports.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. No total gathering count is supplied. Reported arrests (including more than ten activists in S028) are detainee counts, not turnout.
tactic: Activists assembled for a planned march; reports say police surrounded the squares, blocked the route and the march was stopped before it began or proceeded.

title.summary: The reports distinguish an intended march for political prisoners and women vendors from the separate PRA-JA political march earlier that day.

start_date.summary: Both sources place this separate attempted action on 28 January 2023.

end_date.summary: The intended march was prevented or halted before it proceeded; the gathering’s end time is not reported.

location.summary: The reports place the action around Largo das Heroínas/Largo da Independência in Luanda; S028 identifies the intended route toward the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights.

scope.summary: The gathering and planned route were in Luanda.

organizer.summary: S028 identifies activists and quotes Adolfo Campos as an organizer; no organization is named in the read scope.

demands.summary: The demands concern political-prisoner release and treatment of women vendors; S028 additionally reports anti-poverty, prices and health demands.

demand_text.summary: The organizer’s demands include release of political prisoners, action on poverty, lower basic-goods prices and improved health services; the article also reports demands concerning street vendors.

demand_target.summary: The described demands call for action by Angolan authorities or changes to domestic policy.

participants_original.summary: Neither report gives a total attendance figure.

participants_min.summary: No numerical lower bound on total attendance is reported.

participants_max.summary: No numerical upper bound on total attendance is reported.

participants_estimate.summary: No crowd estimate is given; detainee counts cannot be substituted for turnout.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The reported arrests do not count everyone assembled, and neither source gives a total, so 50 or more is unverified.

tactic.summary: The group gathered for a planned march that police reportedly prevented before it proceeded.

protester_violence.summary: S028 attributes to a witness a claim that participants had not initiated aggression; the limited statement does not establish a complete account, so value remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Arrests and police action preventing/dispersing the gathering are reported; accommodation, beatings, ignore, killings and shootings remain unknown.

eligibility.summary: Demand and domestic-state target are reported, but attendance remains below the verified 50-person threshold.

notes: Kept separate from E001 because S029 describes a second action hours later with different demands. S029 is retrospective and does not name the source behind this passage; S028 is the local on-site report. S019, which reports similar arrests, is excluded from evidence because it explicitly credits held source S001 (DW África).
open_questions: Did 50 or more people assemble before the march was stopped?
Can a contemporaneous independent account confirm the second action and clarify how it relates to S028 and the retrospective S029 passage?
When did the gathering end, and were there state responses beyond the reported arrests and dispersal?
